newsitem.title: GERMANY: Japan Pill report step in right direction-Schering.
newsitem.headline: Japan Pill report step in right direction-Schering.

text.p: German drug manufacturer Schering AG said on Wednesday that a Japanese government report saying oral contraceptive pills were safe was a "step in the right direction" towards lifting the ban on the Pill in Japan.

At the same time, a Schering spokeswoman disputed a 500 million pound valuation of the Japanese oral contraceptive market in Wednesday's Financial Times newspaper, saying the true value of the market was "much lower".

Schering is a major manufacturer of oral contraceptives, which have been banned in Japan since their introduction 30 years ago. The group said it expects a full decision on whether the ban will be lifted by the middle of this year.
There are three committees in Japan which are examining the issue, the spokeswoman said.

The first committee is the New Drug Investigation Committee. A sub-committee of this panel, the Combination Drug Committee, which examines the medicinal aspect of the drug, gave its approval on November 19, Schering said.
The second committee is called the Special Committee, which examines ethical and moral aspects of the issue, which gave its approval on Tuesday.

The final committee is the Standing Committee, which examines general health issues, and Schering said it does not know when this committee will report, but said it expects a decision by the middle of the year.
Schering said it was one of up to 10 companies who had applied for approval for low-hormone pills, and said that it was seeking approval for its Triquilar combination Pill product.
